candidate.educational_objective: Interpret basophilia as a nonspecific finding that may require further evaluation.

options.A: Basophilia is nonspecific and can occur with hypersensitivity or inflammatory states and with myeloproliferative disorders, so persistent elevation requires clinical evaluation.
options.B: Basophilia is always a benign normal variant and never needs evaluation.
options.C: Basophilia proves an acute bacterial infection.
options.D: Basophilia is diagnostic of a single allergic disorder.

candidate.rationale: Basophils participate in immediate hypersensitivity and inflammatory responses. Basophilia is nonspecific and may occur with hypersensitivity or inflammation as well as myeloproliferative neoplasms; persistent basophilia therefore requires interpretation in the full clinical and hematologic context.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Basophilia can accompany allergic/inflammatory conditions and myeloproliferative disease and is not diagnostic by itself.
candidate.source_locator: Clinical significance and etiologies—hypersensitivity/inflammation and myeloproliferative disorders
candidate.stem: A client has persistent basophilia on repeated complete blood counts. Which statement by the nurse is most accurate?
